Fix a race condition. If a dataflow worker is waiting for new work (flag==WAITING, waiting on sema down), and then the system is stopped (stopMALdataflow()), the flag is set to FINISHING and the semaphore is "upped".  The worker then first set the flag to RUNNING and then checked whether it was time to exit, making the cleanup code do the wrong thing (based on the flag). Instead, the worker needs to first check whether it needs to exit (leaving the flag unchanged) and if not, set the flag to RUNNING.  Then the cleanup code should do the right thing.

Fix a race condition. If a dataflow worker is waiting for new work (flag==WAITING, waiting on sema down), and then the system is stopped (stopMALdataflow()), the flag is set to FINISHING and the semaphore is "upped".  The worker then first set the flag to RUNNING and then checked whether it was time to exit, making the cleanup code do the wrong thing (based on the flag). Instead, the worker needs to first check whether it needs to exit (leaving the flag unchanged) and if not, set the flag to RUNNING.  Then the cleanup code should do the right thing.

Fix a race condition. If a dataflow worker is waiting for new work (flag==WAITING, waiting on sema down), and then the system is stopped (stopMALdataflow()), the flag is set to FINISHING and the semaphore is "upped".  The worker then first set the flag to RUNNING and then checked whether it was time to exit, making the cleanup code do the wrong thing (based on the flag). Instead, the worker needs to first check whether it needs to exit (leaving the flag unchanged) and if not, set the flag to RUNNING.  Then the cleanup code should do the right thing.

The worker then first set the flag to RUNNING and then checked whether it was time to exit, making the cleanup code do the wrong thing (based on the flag). Instead, the worker needs to first check whether it needs to exit (leaving the flag unchanged) and if not, set the flag to RUNNING.  Then the cleanup code should do the right thing.

Fix a race condition. If a dataflow worker is waiting for new work (flag==WAITING, waiting on sema down), and then the system is stopped (stopMALdataflow()), the flag is set to FINISHING and the semaphore is "upped".  The worker then first set the flag to RUNNING and then checked whether it was time to exit, making the cleanup code do the wrong thing (based on the flag). Instead, the worker needs to first check whether it needs to exit (leaving the flag unchanged) and if not, set the flag to RUNNING.  Then the cleanup code should do the right thing.

example_commits.subject: Don't allocate an extra block when allocating a large one. We needed to fix the size check so that no overflow occurs, then we don't need the extra block.
Buffer reads when using block streams. This also fixes interrupt propagation from client to server when using UNIX domain sockets. (grafted from 7b55d07971fb39850cf9910a31bd068f865598e5)

Fix a race condition. If a dataflow worker is waiting for new work (flag==WAITING, waiting on sema down), and then the system is stopped (stopMALdataflow()), the flag is set to FINISHING and the semaphore is "upped".  The worker then first set the flag to RUNNING and then checked whether it was time to exit, making the cleanup code do the wrong thing (based on the flag). Instead, the worker needs to first check whether it needs to exit (leaving the flag unchanged) and if not, set the flag to RUNNING.  Then the cleanup code should do the right thing.
